repair_arguments: For |x| < 2^(e+1), a square has upper exponent 2e+1. Two factors use e1+e2+1. Same-sign addition uses max(e1,e2)+1; opposed signs need no carry but nonzero/sign classification still needs its independent proof.
An exact input exponent e gives |x| >= 2^e, hence |1/x| <= 2^-e and an upper exponent -e. An input upper bound alone cannot bound the reciprocal above.

For an integer approximation a with one-unit error, magnitude lies in [|a|-1, |a|+1] times its positive scale. An all-ones center reaches the next upper binade; exactness requires both closed endpoints in one binade.

For rational scale r, ceil(log2(|r|)) plus the input upper exponent bounds the product. Exact input binades remain exact under power-of-two scales. Whole rounding/offset arithmetic precedes narrowing.

Compatible inexact upper exponents are ordered by minimum; an exact exponent supplies a lower boundary and cannot exceed any compatible upper exponent. Publication rereads the atomic state on every failed compare-exchange.

The Verus model now expresses these upper-bound premises instead of leaving inexact exponents unconstrained. The checked production transforms are connected by call_ensures; callers still owe valid incoming mathematical certificates.

remaining_source_derived_work.area: Scaled-view monotonicity at the lower exponent limit
remaining_source_derived_work.observation: Real::structural_facts recomputes its scaled upper exponent from the underlying Computable fact. The shared magnitude helper returns None when the rounded result is below i32::MIN. A stronger underlying bound can therefore leave the representable field after a negative scale offset, even though the previously published coarser upper bound remains mathematically valid.
remaining_source_derived_work.proposed_witness: For the mathematical base value 2^i32::MIN, an inexact upper exponent i32::MIN+1 followed by its exact exponent i32::MIN are compatible stronger facts. A Real view scaled by 1/2 first has representable upper exponent i32::MIN, then the helper calculates i32::MIN-1 and returns None. Use a compact Offset graph and independently valid publication certificates so the fixture requires no 2^31-bit integer allocation; test both signs, dyadic/non-dyadic scales and round-trip views.
